name: tovel
author: time-agent
description: tovel v3. Clue "L/S/x/k/n": L = days in the month (28-31), S = the column the 1st falls in (0 = Monday), x = a capital letter, k = 2..6, n = a date. The answer is that month's page: week rows of seven cells, the first row starting in column S, the dates 1..L in reading order, and EVERY date carrying a capital letter (token = the date immediately followed by its letter, e.g. "17B"). A weekday header line is allowed and ignored (any line containing no digit is skipped); whitespace and blank lines are free. RULE: score 1 iff the page is exactly right AND the dates d such that d and d+2 BOTH carry x, the day in between (d+1) does NOT carry x, and d falls on Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday number exactly k, AND the earliest of them is n - i.e. "x, something else, x - inside the same school week (Mon+Wed, Tue+Thu, Wed+Fri) - exactly k times, and the first time is the nth". WHY v3 (the v2 leak, measured in run lad-tovel-v2-1): v2 counted a pair whatever sat between the two days, so a SOLID STRIPE of x manufactured a counted pair on every Mon/Tue/Wed it covered; a stripe of the right length therefore scored 1 with no idea of the rule. tovel1a (opus-lowdemo) hill-climbed exactly that: "letter C runs from day E for as long as it takes to cover W(D) working days", W = {2:4, 3:7, 4:8, 5:9, 6:12}, 88 % final on 2 demos, and its own note calls the table "not a rule a person could ever guess"; tovel1b (opus-theorist) shipped the same witness restricted to the (k, weekday) cells it had measured (34 % of presented, 62 % of answered, 45 % skipped) and never decoded k. Neither player stated the rule; mean 61 %, and the v1 (days,start,k) replay leak stayed shut (1b: "my accepted grids look nothing like the reference ones"). Measured here on 600 fresh clues: the stripe with a per-k best-length table scores 87.50 % against v2 and 0.00 % against v3, at EVERY length 3..16, and 0.00 % with 1/2/3/5 scattered extra x's added. THE FIX is one clause a 12-year-old already assumes: "with a day in between" means the day in between is something else. A solid stripe now has x in the middle of every pair and counts nothing. What still scores without the rule is an ALTERNATING run x . x . x . x from day n with the length tuned per (k, weekday of n): 45.33 % with a per-k table, 57.33 % with a (k, weekday) table - and that is honest, because building it means the player has found the anchor, the distance 2 AND the empty day in between; only the Mon/Tue/Wed clause is missing, and the length table absorbs it. Per k that attack scores 97.7 / 74.1 / 64.0 / 40.0 / 9.5 % at k = 2/3/4/5/6: the long months run out before an every-other-day run can collect six counted pairs, so the large-k clues can only be answered by someone who knows which pairs count. SECOND CHANGE (generate only): the clue's first day n is now drawn as the max of three uniform draws over the days that still leave room for k non-adjacent counted starts, i.e. n sits late in the month. The every-other-day template needs about 14k/3 days of room; the rule itself needs only about 7k/2, because counted starts may be packed Mon+Wed inside one week. Pushing n late therefore starves the template without touching the rule: the (k, weekday) table drops from 72.2 % (uniform n) to 57.3 % (late n), at the cost of shrinking the clue space from 927 to 765 distinct (L,S,k,n) classes and lifting the demo-replay-with-letters-renamed transfer within one (L,S,k) triple from 11.5 % to 24.7 % - which is harmless, because a player only ever holds six demos, i.e. six of the ~140 triples. HEADER: deliberately still randomised over three styles (the scorer skips any line with no digit). tovel1b read the varying header as "the grader isn't comparing text" and it is right: that is a free, true hint that the grader is a predicate over content, it cannot leak anything about the rule, and making it uniform would only tempt players back toward the replay strategies v2 closed. INTENDED DISCOVERY PATH (private): (1) one demo shows a calendar page and "L/S" is its shape - the first row holds 7-S dates; kid-easy, and nothing scores until it is right. (2) x names the letter being counted; the other letters are noise. (3) n is a date, and in every demo day n carries x and so does day n+2, with something else in between - the relation. (4) k counts them; which pairs count? solve() guarantees that in EVERY demo each rival count differs from k (x next door, a week apart, three apart, two apart anywhere, two apart in a week row, the number of x's, the same relation for any letter, cells-not-pairs, x.x anywhere, x.x in a week row, and - the new one - THE v2 RULE, two apart with the gap free). (5) two exclusions are shown positively in every demo: a run x x x starting on a Mon/Tue/Wed that does NOT count (99.5 % of demos; 89.6 % have one BEFORE day n, so a player using the v2 rule computes the wrong first day), and a pair reaching the weekend (Thu start) plus one stepping over the week break (Sat/Sun start) (95.5 %); some non-counting pair sits before day n in 93.8 % (measured over 3000 demos). Hypothesis-elimination surrogate over 840 hand-built "count a relation between marked days" expressions (distance 1-7 x 10 weekday windows x 3 gap conditions x this-letter/any-letter x pairs/cells, 752 distinct behaviours): 3-21 survive one demo, 1 survives two - v1 needed 3-6 demos, so v3 is markedly fairer as well as harder. WITNESSES (600 fresh clues each): empty, spaces, newlines, "0", "1", "x", "1"*100, a 4000-char junk string, the clue itself, a bare date grid with no letters, an all-x page, a one-letter page - all 0.00 %; best constant answer 1.00 %; tuned random lettering 0.08-0.96 % at densities 0.20-0.80 (v1: 3.5-16.4 %). Wrong-relation constructors on a correct page honouring the clue's first day: next door 0.00 %, three apart 0.00 %, a week apart 3.82 %, two apart anywhere 12.33 %, two apart in a week row 17.67 %, THE v2 RULE (two apart, Mon-Wed, gap free) 33.33 %, x.x anywhere 15.00 %, x.x in a week row 20.67 %, the true rule 100.00 %; ignoring the clue's first day, all of those fall to 0.00-7.00 %. Shape attacks on a page with the correct count: one row, one token per line, zero-padded dates, an extra day, a dropped day, lower case, "17 B" instead of "17B" - all 0.00 %; header/no header, tabs and blank lines 100 % (robust about form, strict about content); a page laid out from column 0 scores 11 % = exactly the S=0 clues. The scorer never raises and never returns a non-binary value on 20000 random junk strings (worst 0.05 ms), agrees with an independent re-implementation of the stated rule on 9000 well-formed mutated answers with 0 disagreements, and is 431 chars. solve() scores 1 on 3000/3000 fresh seeds (92 ms average, 226 ms worst; solution <= 175 chars), randomises the header style, the alphabet (4-5 letters), the chain structure and the decoy placement, and re-parses its own output before returning it. Human-designed for the "everyday time and place" direction: the object is a family calendar, the measurement has no name, and recognising the calendar is necessary but nowhere near sufficient.
generate:
def generate(seed):
    r = random.Random(seed)
    L = r.choice([28, 29, 30, 31, 30, 31])
    S = r.randrange(7)
    x = r.choice(string.ascii_uppercase)
    k = r.randint(2, 6)
    E = [d for d in range(1, L - 1) if (d - 1 + S) % 7 < 3]
    F = []
    for j, d0 in enumerate(E):          # first days with room for k non-adjacent starts
        t = 0
        p = -9
        for d in E[j:]:
            if d - p > 1:
                t += 1
                p = d
        if t >= k:
            F.append(d0)
    i = max(r.randrange(len(F)), r.randrange(len(F)), r.randrange(len(F)))
    return "%d/%d/%s/%d/%d" % (L, S, x, k, F[i])   # n sits late: starves the x.x.x template
solve:
def sel(g, S, x):
    # THE RULE: x, something else, x - starting on a Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday
    return [i for i in range(len(g) - 2) if g[i] == g[i + 2] == x != g[i + 1] and (i + S) % 7 < 3]


def cnts(g, S, x):
    # counted, rivals that must NOT equal k, wrong-day starts, blocked starts
    L = len(g)
    P = [i for i in range(L - 2) if g[i] == g[i + 2] == x]
    C = sel(g, S, x)
    D = [i for i in P if g[i + 1] != x and (i + S) % 7 > 2]
    B = [i for i in P if g[i + 1] == x and (i + S) % 7 < 3]
    H = (sum(1 for i in range(L - 1) if g[i] == g[i + 1] == x),
         len(P), sum(1 for i in P if (i + S) % 7 < 5),
         sum(1 for i in range(L - 7) if g[i] == g[i + 7] == x), g.count(x),
         sum(1 for i in range(L - 2) if g[i] == g[i + 2] != g[i + 1] and (i + S) % 7 < 3),
         sum(1 for i in range(L - 3) if g[i] == g[i + 3] == x),
         sum(1 for i in P if g[i + 1] != x),
         sum(1 for i in P if g[i + 1] != x and (i + S) % 7 < 5),
         len({j for i in C for j in (i, i + 2)}))
    return C, H, D, B


def render(g, S, r):
    h = r.choice(["Mo Tu We Th Fr Sa Su", "MON TUE WED THU FRI SAT SUN", "M T W T F S S"]).split()
    cs = [""] * S + ["%d%s" % (i + 1, g[i]) for i in range(len(g))]
    while len(cs) % 7:
        cs.append("")
    o = [" ".join(w.rjust(3) for w in h).rstrip()]
    for j in range(0, len(cs), 7):
        o.append(" ".join(c.rjust(3) for c in cs[j:j + 7]).rstrip())
    return "\n".join(o)


def chk(s, L, S, x, k, f):
    R = [l.split() for l in s.split("\n") if any(h.isdigit() for h in l)]
    T = [t for r in R for t in r]
    if (len(T) != L or len(R[0]) != 7 - S or not 0 < len(R[-1]) < 8
            or any(len(r) != 7 for r in R[1:-1])
            or any(t[:-1] != str(i + 1) or t[-1] <= "9" for i, t in enumerate(T))):
        return 0
    C = sel([t[-1] for t in T], S, x)
    return len(C) == k and C[0] == f


def solve(clue):
    a = clue.split("/"); L = int(a[0]); S = int(a[1]); x = a[2]; k = int(a[3]); f = int(a[4]) - 1
    r = random.Random(clue)
    po = [c for c in string.ascii_uppercase if c != x]
    sl = [i for i in range(L - 2) if (i + S) % 7 < 3 and i > f + 1]
    room = []   # how much room each slot leaves
    for i in sl:
        t = 0; p = i
        for j in sl:
            if j > p + 1:
                t += 1; p = j
        room.append(t)
    for att in range(1600):
        w = 4 if att < 700 else 3 if att < 1000 else 2 if att < 1300 else 1 if att < 1500 else 0
        ot = r.sample(po, r.randint(3, 4))
        g = [r.choice(ot) for _ in range(L)]
        ch = [f]
        while len(ch) < k:      # never two counted starts side by side
            av = [i for i, t in zip(sl, room) if i > ch[-1] + 1 and t >= k - len(ch) - 1]
            if not av:
                break
            ch.append(av[0] if r.random() < 0.5 else r.choice(av[:3]))
        if len(ch) < k:
            continue
        for i in ch:
            g[i] = x; g[i + 2] = x
        mv = [[(i, i + 1, i + 2) for i in range(L - 2) if (i + S) % 7 < 3]]   # x x x
        r.shuffle(mv[0])
        mv[0].sort(key=lambda p: not (w > 3 and p[0] < f))
        for want in ((3, 4), (5, 6)):       # weekend-reaching / week-break decoys
            c2 = [(i, i + 2) for i in range(L - 2) if (i + S) % 7 in want]
            r.shuffle(c2)
            c2.sort(key=lambda p: (not (w > 3 and p[0] < f),
                                   min(abs(p[0] - c) for c in ch) > 3))
            mv.append(c2)
        mv += [[(i, i + 1) for i in range(L - 1)], [(i, i + 7) for i in range(L - 7)]]
        r.shuffle(mv[3]); r.shuffle(mv[4])
        for c2 in mv:
            for p in c2:
                sv = [g[i] for i in p]
                for i in p:
                    g[i] = x
                C = sel(g, S, x)
                if len(C) == k and C[0] == f:
                    break
                for i, v in zip(p, sv):
                    g[i] = v
        fr = [i for i in sl if x not in (g[i], g[i + 1], g[i + 2])]
        r.shuffle(fr)
        for i in fr[:2]:          # another letter, two apart
            c = r.choice(ot)
            g[i] = c; g[i + 2] = c
            if g[i + 1] == c:
                g[i + 1] = r.choice([q for q in ot if q != c])
        C, H, D, B = cnts(g, S, x)
        if len(C) != k or C[0] != f or any(h == k for h in H) or len(set(g)) < 4:
            continue
        p1 = [i for i in D if (i + S) % 7 == 3]
        p2 = [i for i in D if (i + S) % 7 in (5, 6)]
        if w and (not B or not p1 or not p2):
            continue
        if w > 2 and (min(abs(i - c) for i in p1 for c in C) > 3
                      or min(abs(i - c) for i in p2 for c in C) > 3):
            continue
        if w > 3 and f > 0 and not [i for i in B + D if i < f]:
            continue
        if w > 1 and g.count(x) > (0.30 + 0.035 * k) * L:
            continue
        s = render(g, S, r)
        if chk(s, L, S, x, k, f):
            return s
    return ""
